newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran leader calls for crackdown on corruption.
newsitem.headline: Iran leader calls for crackdown on corruption.

text.p: Iran's supreme leader on Wednesday called for stepping up the fight against corruption and influence peddling, rejecting suggestions that tough action might discourage investors.

"There are people aiming to create a new privileged class in the Islamic Republic of Iran through connections, nominations, clever means...and access to public wealth," Ayatollah Ali Khamenei said in remarks broadcast on Tehran radio.

"When we say this should be countered, some people quickly express concern that such action would endanger the security of investment. No, gentlemen, this would instead help investment," Khamenei added. He did not say who had expressed concern.

"Our judiciary, our lawmakers and other state bodies target those who break laws. Why should people who do not break laws be afraid? Let violators be afraid. Sinful people should feel insecure in our Islamic system," Khamenei said.

Iranian leaders have called for tough action against corruption following a series of trials for embezzlement and fraud at state agencies and banks in the past few years that have featured prominently in the local media.
The calls come at a time when state economic officials are seeking to encourage investment, including much needed foreign capital.
Iranians have traditionally tended to invest in real estate or sought quick gains by dealing in gold or foreign currencies instead of investing in the stock market or industry.
Analysts say this reflects investors' concerns about a complicated tax system and other regulations which are sometimes applied arbitrarily.

The anti-corruption drive has also taken a political turn with hardline and conservative Islamic newspapers and parliament deputies calling for probes against moderate officials close to outgoing President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and president-elect Mohammad Khatami.
Khatami, who is due to take over on August 3, defeated the conservatives' candidate, parliament speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, by a landslide in May.
